name: Ferroelectric film polar only above a critical thickness (dimensionless)
question: Is the direction of the polarization inherited when a film is cleaved below its critical thickness and grows again?
assumptions: Landau-Ginzburg-Devonshire theory of a second-order ferroelectric with in-plane polarization (no depolarizing field) and Landau-Khalatnikov relaxation, in units of the correlation length, the relaxation time and the bulk polarization
the extrapolation length delta = xi (delta > 0 suppresses the polarization at the faces); no material value of delta/xi is published in the sources read
growth by deposition on both faces at the rate 0.1; division by cleaving at 1.6 L_c
thermal noise of intensity 3e-3 per unit thickness

provenance.source: R. Kretschmer and K. Binder, Phys. Rev. B 20, 1065 (1979); D. R. Tilley and B. Zeks, Solid State Commun. 49, 823 (1984); P. Chandra and P. B. Littlewood, arXiv cond-mat/0609347
